posts.title: Achyutananda Dasa
posts.excerpt: The story of Mahapurusha Achyutananda Dasa, one of Odisha's five Panchasakha saints and a knower of jyotish-astrology, and his Shunya philosophy.
posts.body:
Chaitanya Mahaprabhu had five Mahapurusa (great men) disciples in Odisha called Pancasakha. Pancha means five and Sakha means friends — the five friends being Jasovanta Dasa, Jagannath Dasa, Balarama Dasa, Shishu Ananta Dasa and Achyutananda Dasa. The great spiritual leader Chaitanya Mahaprabhu referred to these five disciples as Panchasakha and stated that they are like his Pancha Atma, i.e., five souls (Atma-Tattva), in no way lesser than some of the Avatars of Vishnu.

From the Shunya Samhita of Achyutananda Dasa we learn each Panchasakha had a certain expertise and knowledge:

- Jasovanta Dasa: procedure for proper rituals and sacrifices
- Shishu Ananta Dasa: drawing lines — yantra, vastu and mantra sastra
- Achyutananda Dasa: knower of past-present-future, jyotish-astrology
- Balarama Dasa: tattva bhava — Samkhya sastra
- Jagannath Dasa: bhakti bhava — divine love

Born in the Cuttack district of Odisha, **Sri Achyutananda's** birthplace was Tilakana, a village situated at the confluence of the Luna and Chitrotpala rivers, both branches of the Mahanadi. Scholars estimate his birth year to fall between 1480 and 1505 on a Magha Sukla Ekadasi, corresponding to the twenty-first regnal year of the Gajapati king Purushottam Deva. His parents were Padmavati and Dinabandhu Khuntia, and his maternal grandfather was Gopinath Mohanty, who served as a scribe at the Jagannath Temple in Puri. His parents, who had been childless for a long period, had been praying to Lord Jagannath for a child. One night, his father experienced a vision of Garuda, the eagle vehicle of Vishnu, presenting him with a child. The following morning, he went to the temple and offered prayers at the Garuda Khamba (a pillar in front of the Jagannath temple) in gratitude. Two accounts exist regarding Achyutananda's birth: one suggests Dinabandhu Khuntia found a divine newborn there, while the other posits that Padma Devi conceived a divine child shortly after this vision.

Mahapurusha Achyutananda is believed to have been born through special grace or divine intervention, linked to Lord Jagannath himself (as suggested by "Vibhuti Yoga" in the Shrimad Bhagavad Gita). This divine association is reflected in his name, Achyuta, interpreted as "A" (Shri Vishnu) and "chyuta" (created from). He is sometimes also called "Achyuti," an Oriya term signifying "one who has no fall."

The Panchasakha played a crucial role in making ancient Hindu scriptures accessible to the people of Udra Desha (Odisha) by translating them into straightforward prose. Among them, Shri Achyutananda Das stands out as the most productive writer, credited with numerous texts known as Pothis, purportedly authored across multiple incarnations. Revered as the Mahapurusha, signifying "a great man," Achyutananda was a practitioner of Shunya Sadhana who amassed extensive knowledge encompassing spirituality, Ayurveda, various scientific disciplines, and social norms.

## Panchasakha Ideology

### Shunya Purusha

*nahi tahara rupa varna, adarsha avarna ta chinha.*
*tahaku brahma boli kahi, sunya brahmhati se bolai.*

It has no shape, no colour, it is invisible and ideal, without a name. This Brahman is called Shunya Brahman. The Panchasakhas believed in a concept of God as Sunya (emptiness, void, zero) called Shunya Purusha or Shunya Brahman. This Shunya signifies a transcendental principle that eludes the conceptual nexus applied to human thinking as described in the Upanishads.

Achyutananda's culminating work is the Shunya Samhita, where he discusses this philosophy in depth.

*sunyara akara viira sunyara vicara, sunye thai dekha vira e sacaracara.*
*dekha e sacaracara sunyare prakasha, sunyu ude hoichanti sunyare vilase.*

Look at the shunya by placing yourself in shunya, and meditate on mahashunya. Shunya itself is the form, the ground of all discriminating knowledge. Look at the whole world from the pedestal of Shunya; you will find everything manifested in the Shunya — everything arises out of Shunya and everything flourishes in the Shunya Brahman.

This philosophy is not the Shunya of the Buddhists, as it is not empty but full — sometimes even called the Purna Shunya (the full/complete void).

The Panchasakhas project the deity Jagannath as the embodiment of the Shunya Purusha. Achyutananda uses a classical concept of Vaishnavism that holds both form and formless aspects of God together. This is seen in his statement from the Gurubhakti Gita:

*dui je dinare paksi udikari jai, dui je chaksure sehi samsare khelai.*
*ekaje na thile kana dui gale andha, enukari nirguna saguna sehi bheda.*

A bird can only fly with both wings. It can have perfect vision with both eyes. In the absence of one, it becomes one-eyed, and in the absence of both, it is totally blind. Thus, like two eyes, Nirguna (God perceived as formless) and Saguna (God perceived with form) are chained together.

Mahapurusha Achyutananda's Shunya Samhita presents a fascinating account of the Panchasakha's origins, linking them to the Mahabharata's Dwapara-Yuga. The text explains that Panchasakha literally means "five mates or friends." This narrative details how, as Lord Krishna prepared to leave the mortal realm at the close of the Mahabharata era, Nilakantheswara Mahadeva (Lord Shiva, residing in Puri with a blue throat from his act of saving the world from poison) appeared and spoke with Krishna. Shiva disclosed that Krishna's companions Dama, Sudama, Srivatsa, Subala, and Subahu would reincarnate in the Kali-Yuga, becoming known as Ananta, Achyutananda, Jagannatha, Balarama, and Yasovanta. Therefore, those who adhere to the Panchasakha tradition believe these five saints were the closest confidantes of Lord Krishna during the Dwapara-Yuga and were reborn in the Kali-Yuga to continue their service to him.

Mahapurusha Achyutananda established numerous spiritual and energetic centers, known as 'Gadis, across eastern India (the former regions of Anga, Banga, Kalinga, Magadha) and parts of Nepal. These Gadis served as hubs for spiritual practices, teachings, asceticism, and offered various forms of support to spiritual seekers — examples include Nemal, Kakatpur, Garoi, and Jobra Ghat (a riverbank in Cuttack).

**References:**

1. [Odisha Review, June 2014](https://magazines.odisha.gov.in/Orissareview/2014/Jun/engpdf/115-119.pdf)
2. Jamini Upadesa Sutra — Pt Sanjay Rath
3. [Wikipedia: Achyutananda Dasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achyutananda_Dasa)
4. [Odisha Annual Reference 2011](https://magazines.odisha.gov.in/orissaannualreference/ORA-2011/pdf/43-46.pdf)

**Om tat sat**

posts.title: Prostate Cancer
posts.excerpt: A follow-up medical astrology study using Kharesa and Nara Chakra nakshatra mapping to analyze 18 AA-rated prostate cancer charts, finding a 95% affliction correlation.
posts.body:
*Disclaimer: Please be advised that I am not a medical professional. This article presents the results of my personal academic research in Vedic astrology related to prostate cancer. The information provided herein is for informational and academic interest only and should not be interpreted as medical advice. Readers are strongly encouraged to consult with qualified healthcare professionals for any health concerns, diagnoses, or treatment options. The application and interpretation of astrological insights are at the reader's discretion.*

**Prostate cancer** is a malignant tumor that develops in the prostate gland, a walnut-sized organ located below the bladder in men. The prostate produces seminal fluid that nourishes and transports sperm (so the primary karaka ~ significator is Shukra/Venus).

**The Biological Causes of Prostate Cancer**

- Genetic Mutations and DNA Damage (karaka/significator ~ Surya/Sun)
- Hormonal Influences (karaka/significator ~ Shukra/Venus)
- Chronic Inflammation (karaka/significator ~ Surya/Sun)

**Survival vs. Mortality**

The single most important factor determining survival is how early the cancer is detected. Localized prostate cancer confined to the gland has a near 100% five-year survival rate. Once cancer spreads to nearby tissues, survival rates drop somewhat but remain favorable. Early detection through PSA screening and digital rectal exams can identify cancer while it's still curable.

**Symptoms of Prostate Cancer**

In its early stages, when the cancer is still confined to the prostate gland, most men experience no noticeable symptoms. The cancer is usually discovered through:

- Elevated PSA (prostate-specific antigen) levels detected during routine blood work
- Abnormalities felt during a digital rectal exam
- Incidental findings during imaging or procedures for other conditions

**When to See a Doctor**

You should consult a healthcare provider if you experience:

- Any urinary symptoms that are new, worsening, or interfering with daily life
- Blood in your urine or semen
- Persistent bone pain, especially in the back or hips
- Unexplained weight loss or fatigue

Additionally, men should discuss prostate cancer screening with their doctor, particularly if they are:

- Age 50 or older (for average-risk men)
- Age 45 or older with a family history of prostate cancer
- Age 40 or older with multiple family members diagnosed with prostate cancer at young ages

## Research Background

This investigation extends my earlier research into the astrological analysis of Alzheimer's disease, wherein the concept of Kharesa (Khara Navamsa) was established as a foundational framework for medical astrological analysis. While the application of Kharesa principles has been detailed in my previous work, the present study specifically focuses on the application of Nara Chakra as a refined diagnostic tool for anatomical specificity in disease prediction.

The Nara Chakra system, comprehensively documented in Pt. Sanjay Rath's Parashara Jyotisha Course (PJC) and his seminal work *Brihat Nakshatra*, provides a sophisticated mapping methodology that assigns specific human anatomical structures to the 27 nakshatras based on an individual's janma (birth) nakshatra. This research investigates whether afflictions to nakshatras governing the prostate gland, particularly when evaluated through the Kharesa framework, demonstrate consistent patterns across prostate cancer cases.

## Methodology

**Sample Selection**

The study employs a carefully curated dataset of 18 birth charts, all carrying AA ratings from Astrodatabank, ensuring the highest level of birth data reliability. The selection criteria required a confirmed medical diagnosis of prostate cancer. The sample was intentionally balanced to include:

- 9 cases (50%) of individuals who achieved recovery from prostate cancer
- 9 cases (50%) of individuals who succumbed to the disease

This balanced approach allows for comparative analysis of survival outcomes, though the primary focus remains on disease manifestation rather than prognosis.

**Analytical Framework**

The analysis integrates two primary astrological concepts:

1. **Kharesa (Khara Navamsa) Analysis:** The foundational affliction assessment framework established in my prior research, which identifies malefic influences that contribute to disease manifestation.
2. **Nara Chakra Mapping:** A nakshatra-based anatomical correlation system that allows for precise identification of vulnerable body systems based on birth nakshatra and subsequent afflictions.

**Hypothesis**

**Primary Hypothesis**: If the nakshatra or nakshatra lord corresponding to the prostate gland shows affliction through Khara Navamsa principles, then prostate cancer manifestation can be astrologically identified with high consistency.

**Secondary Observation**: Benefic influences, particularly from Brihaspati (Jupiter), correlate with recovery outcomes. (Note: Complete delineation of protective factors requires traditional guru-shishya instruction or formal study through established pedagogical frameworks such as the PJC course, and is therefore not elaborated in this public research summary.)

## Results

The analysis yielded remarkably consistent findings:

**95% correlation was observed across the sampled charts:** In 17 of 18 cases, either the nakshatra corresponding to the prostate gland or its ruling lord demonstrated clear affliction according to Khara Navamsa principles. Case 'Pros-18' has a weak correlation; however, prostate cancer was not the primary cause of the subject's demise.

This high correlation rate establishes a robust empirical foundation for the integrated application of Kharesa and Nara Chakra concepts in medical astrological diagnosis.

## Conclusion

This study establishes a robust empirical foundation for the application of Nara Chakra principles in prostate cancer analysis, demonstrating very high correlation between nakshatra afflictions and disease manifestation across 18 AA-rated cases. The integration of Kharesa and Nara Chakra concepts proves to be a powerful framework for achieving anatomical specificity in medical astrological diagnosis.

The findings validate traditional Jyotish wisdom regarding the nakshatra-anatomy correspondence system while opening pathways for more refined medical astrological research. The question of achieving even greater determinism in astrological analysis remains an important frontier for continued investigation.

*Author's Note: This research represents ongoing work in medical astrology and is part of a broader investigation into the astrological correlates of specific disease states. Previous publications include research on Alzheimer's disease utilizing similar methodological frameworks.*

posts.title: Children: D7 Varga
posts.excerpt: How the Saptamsa (D7) divisional chart reveals children, pregnancy, and progeny in Vedic astrology, and the planetary combinations that support or deny them.
posts.body:
The most salient and distinguishing feature of Jyotisa ~ Vedic Astrology compared to any other astrology system is the Vargas ~ divisional charts. The rasi chart (D1) we construct at the time of birth is further used to create more charts called Vargas ~ divisional charts based on mathematical calculations, and each varga represents a specific area of life. Just as a tree trunk divides into its various fruit-bearing branches, so does this division of the main rasi chart into vargas can be visualized. We look at the Rasi chart (D1) to analyze the broad situation and then use the vargas to deep dive into specifics. Though there are many vargas, the shodasvarga system (16 divisionals) is most often talked about, which includes:

- Navamsa (D9) for marriage, intimacy and skills
- Saptamsa (D7) for progeny, parenting and pregnancy
- Chaturthamsa (D4) for properties
- Dasamsa (D10) for work and career
- Dwadasamsa (D12) for parents, uncles-aunts, grandparents

## Saptamsa (D7)

Saptamsa shows pregnancy conditions, children to be born including gender, and what the future of the child is like. It also shows problems in conception, abortion, and miscarriages. However, we check the Rasi chart (D1) first to ascertain karma towards children. For men, the 5th house is analysed, while for women the 9th house is analysed.

Guru ~ Jupiter is karaka (significator) of children, and its condition is to be seen first in Saptamsa to determine if it is conducive to having children.

Saptamsa Lagna is the native's attitude towards their children. Malefics there make one harsh or give no desire of having children. If the Saptamsa Lagna is odd, the first child is seen from the 5th house and subsequent children are seen as the third from there, and so on.

Birth takes place during the dasa of planets having Argala on the Saptamsa Lagna.

Mercury, Saturn and/or Venus are not supportive towards giving children (J.S. 1.4.24). 

Mercury and Saturn are eunuch planets and can deny fertility. Venus is interested in keeping love life going instead of letting one into parenthood, and so can deplete chances for progeny.

Sun, Rahu and Jupiter promise many children, while Moon promises one (J.S. 1.4.25-26).

If there are combinations or aspects involving both planets giving children (Sun, Rahu, Jupiter and Moon) and those denying children (Mercury, Saturn and Venus), then a child will be born later in life (J.S. 1.4.27).

Saturn and Mars together promote adoption of children (J.S. 1.4.28).

There are many more rules we learn in the Parasara Jyotish Course (PJC) which are not known outside the parampara and give incredible results about ascertaining child birth.

**Om ṭat ṣat**

posts.title: Alzheimer's
posts.excerpt: A study exploring correlations between Khara Navamsa, Mangala, and Vayu-tatva planetary influences and Alzheimer's disease across 58 AA-rated natal charts.
posts.body:
*Disclaimer: Please be advised that I am not a medical professional. This article presents the results of my personal academic research in Vedic astrology related to Alzheimer's disease. The information provided herein is for informational and academic interest only and should not be interpreted as medical advice. Readers are strongly encouraged to consult with qualified healthcare professionals for any health concerns, diagnoses, or treatment options. The application and interpretation of astrological insights are at the reader's discretion.*

Alzheimer's disease is a complex neurodegenerative disorder that significantly destroys memory, cognition, and behavior. As one of the most common forms of dementia, its prevalence has increased globally, posing significant challenges for healthcare systems. While the exact causes are still not fully understood, scientists have identified **Amyloid Plaques** and **Tau Tangles** as playing a significant role in its development:

- **Amyloid Plaques**: Imagine sticky clumps of a protein called beta-amyloid that build up between nerve cells in the brain. These plaques disrupt cell function and communication — think of them like roadblocks that prevent brain cells from talking to each other effectively.
- **Tau Tangles**: Inside brain cells, there's another protein called tau that helps stabilize their structure. In Alzheimer's, tau protein becomes tangled into abnormal fibers. These tangles disrupt the transport system within the cell, preventing essential nutrients from moving around, eventually leading to cell death — imagine the cell's internal transport system getting choked up.

Vedic astrology, rooted in ancient Indian tradition, posits that the positions and interactions of graha ~ planets at the time of birth can provide insights into various aspects of an individual's life, including health.

This study seeks to identify the connections between medical findings and astrological principles by analyzing specific planetary configurations in the natal charts of individuals affected by Alzheimer's disease. It aims to identify recurring patterns and explore whether these align with known medical risk factors, offering a unique perspective on the condition's origins.

## Methodology

We can begin examination of a medical or healthcare question by investigating the 64th navamsa, termed Khara navamsa, as mentioned in *Jataka Parijata*. This sensitive area of the birth chart also finds mention in other classics including *Brihat Parasara Hora Shastra*, *Hora Ratnam*, and *Prasna Marga*. While most of the texts discuss results related to transits or longevity, Paramguruji Sanjay Rath teaches this concept with wider application and philosophy, which is part of his PJC course.

I selected 58 AA-rated charts from Astrodatabank. All these subjects specifically suffered from Alzheimer's disease, and other forms of dementia or Parkinson's disease were ruled out during chart selection.

Because Alzheimer's is a neurodegenerative disorder which occurs primarily in old age, the first hypothesis is the influence of:

- Vayu tatva and/or
- Mangala and/or
- Budh/Guru graha

on Khara navamsa.

Vayu tatva graha are degenerating, Mangala rules nerves, and Budh/Guru rule memory, cognition and ability to perform tasks.

This is a necessary but not a sufficient condition to establish the possibility of Alzheimer's disease. 49 of 58 charts complied with condition one, and 7 cases complied with either condition two or three. Only 2 cases did not identify with either of the above conditions. The two outliers were Freeman, Orville and Bailey, Mildred Caroon.

There were two more conditions placed concerning the 6th and 12th house of the navamsa; however, these were secondary and are proprietary to PJC coursework. These conditions are used to further support the above primary hypothesis.

The second hypothesis was for the Rasi chart (D1): Mangala should be afflicted or influenced by Vayu tatva graha, either by placement, aspect or conjunction.

The disease has to manifest physically, and for that to happen, Mangala ~ nerves must suffer degeneration ~ vayu. This is also a necessary but not a sufficient condition, and 51 of 58 charts complied with this condition. Of the remaining 7: in 2 charts the Lagna Lord is very weak, causing loss of intellectual abilities; 1 chart has the influence of Sani on both Mangala's rasi, which is a weak connection but still qualifies; and the other 3 charts have Mangala in a weak condition by being debilitated, MKS being Vara lord. Only the chart of Cutler, Virginia did not seem to present any weakness in D1 based on this condition, though there's one more principle in action based on Vara-Cakra which could justify Alzheimer's in her chart.

Along with the above, in the Rasi chart (D1), either or both of these supporting conditions can be expected to co-exist:

- Weak Surya: indicating low vitality, especially in old age as Vayu graha gets dominant
- Afflicted Aries or 1H or Ju or Me: to indicate possibility of brain conditions

48 of 58 charts complied with both of these conditions. Of the remaining, 4 complied with either condition. In 3 charts, the 4th bhava from Chandra was found to be afflicted. One of the conditions which can lead to Alzheimer's disease is prenatal distress, although it wasn't a primary focus of this study.

There were additional supporting conditions which enabled narrowing down the possibility of the disease. However, these are proprietary to PJC coursework and hence are not discussed.

## Conclusion

This study offers a preliminary exploration into the correlation between astrological indicators and the manifestation of Alzheimer's disease, with a particular focus on Khara Navamsa and planetary influences in both the Navamsa (D9) and Rasi (D1) charts. Through the analysis of 58 AA-rated charts of individuals diagnosed specifically with Alzheimer's, certain recurring astrological patterns emerged — most notably, the influence of Vayu-tatva graha, Mangala, and Budh/Guru in critical chart placements.

While not intended as a diagnostic tool, this study attempts to bridge ancient wisdom with modern medical understanding. The inclusion of PJC methodology enriches the interpretive process, though much of it remains within a specific lineage of teaching.

**Om ṭat ṣat**

posts.title: Conception-Ṇiseka
posts.excerpt: How Jyotisa treats the moment of conception (Ṇiseka) as a muhurta in itself — and why controlling this moment matters more than controlling the birth time.
posts.body:
**Ṇiseka** means fertilization, and various jyotisa texts talk about the moment of fertilization — conception. The texts recommend muhurta-planetary conditions which enable the couple to produce a 'desired' child. We've come across various stories in Hindu mythology which seem out of this world when talking about the birth of children. And though as we are presently, we may not be able to do miracles, certainly jyotisa can help us decide the moment of copulation which would be favorable to the birth of a noble soul. And this moment also guides the pregnancy phase and the events which unfold during this period.

We know from mythology that the great bhakta Prahalada was deeply influenced by Narada's discourses while he was still in his mother's womb, and how the great warrior Abhimanyu learnt about piercing the Chakravyuh from his father Arjuna's narration to his mother while he was still in her womb.

The moment and process of birth are not just incidental or a moment of planning in an adult life — rather these can be carefully crafted events that can shape the future course of one's lineage.

Some people try to control the birth time of a child by asking for a 'perfect' time to have a caesarean surgery. What they often fail to realize is that the good and the bad have already been stamped, and even if they manage to have a 'favorable' time of birth, all the defects that were to be carried onto the child would appear in some manner in certain parts of life. So probably it is better to control conception than birth. When we try to control the birth time, we are trying to play god, which can be counterproductive; however, when we try to control the conception time, we are following the advice of the sages, which is likely to lead to more balanced results.

## Pre-Natal Ceremonies: Garbādhana Samskara

Garbhādhana is the first of the 16 saṃskāras in Hinduism. Garbhādhana = Garbhā (womb) + ādhana (placing). It is a ceremony performed before ṇiseka (conception) for purification of the mind, body and soul. The pre-natal samskaras — Garbādhana, Pumsavana, Ṣeemantonnayana — help with the removal of vices and impurities which are hereditary and acquired due to mistakes committed by parents and other family members.

## Conception: Ṇiseka-Ādhana

Ṇiseka is the moment of copulation, while the moment of conception is termed ādhana. The ṇiseka can be controlled by us, but ādhana may take its own time. Jyotisa texts refer distinctly to ṇiseka and ādhana. While a chart can be cast for ṇiseka anytime, arriving at the moment of ādhana requires further calculations. To understand the difference: modern technology allows for freezing of fertilized embryos — ṇiseka — which can then later be implanted to initiate pregnancy — ādhana.

There are various jyotisa rules to select an appropriate time for ṇiseka (conception); however, to produce a desired child, the most important rule is that a couple should have peace of mind and be happy at the time of conception.

Festival days, Chaturthi, Ashtami, Navami, Chaturdasi, Amavasya and Poornima tithi are to be avoided for conception.

Day time is to be avoided, while night time is to be preferred.

Rohini, Ūttaraphalguni, Ḥasta, Svati, Ānuradha, Ṃula, Ūttaraśada, Srvana, Sathabiśaj, Ūttarabhadrapada, Revati: these nakshatras are best, but one's own Janma, 10th and 19th nakshatra are to be avoided.

Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday are preferred days.

*[a vedic day is sunrise to next sunrise, so 2am on 'Gregorian Thursday night' is still Vedic Wednesday]*

Days from menses are to be chosen carefully, as each one has a specific result to deliver. Example — the thirteenth day favours the birth of a virtuous girl.

The ṇiseka (conception) moment also has a significant impact on the woman who is to bear the child. Example — if the ṇiseka Lagna and the rasi occupied by the Moon be in papa-kartari without any benefic dristi, the woman will either die within the period of pregnancy or parturition. Similarly, there are various combinations to be avoided, and so the ancient royal families employed scholars and jyotisa to determine the appropriate time to conceive children.

*Brihat Parāśara Horā Śhāstra, Brihat Jataka, Kalapraksika, Jataka Parijata, Manusmriti* are some texts which give detailed information about determining the time of conception.

By honoring the principles of Ṇiseka and selecting an auspicious moment for conception, we are not just planning for a child but actively participating in the refinement of our lineage. Vedic tradition reminds us that the true power lies in conscious creation. Just as sunlight nourishes the seeds that blossom into mighty trees, the cosmic alignment present at conception deeply influences the physical, mental, and spiritual attributes of the unborn child.

**Om ṭat ṣat**

**श्रीराम राम रामेति रमे रामे मनोरमे** ।

 **सहस्रनामतत्तुल्यं रामनाम वरानने ॥**

 The Name of Rāma is as Great as the Thousand Names of Viṣṇu.[excerpt from Viṣṇu Sahasranāma] 



### Birth Data Source 

Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa - BālaKāṇḍa - Sarga 18

ततो यज्ञे समाप्ते तु ऋतूनां षट्समत्ययु:।

ततश्च द्वादशे मासे चैत्रे नावमिके तिथौ।।1.18.8।।

नक्षत्रेऽदितिदैवत्ये स्वोच्चसंस्थेषु पञ्चसु।

ग्रहेषु कर्कटे लग्ने वाक्पताविन्दुना सह।।1.18.9।।

प्रोद्यमाने जगन्नाथं सर्वलोकनमस्कृतम्।

कौसल्याऽजनयद्रामं सर्वलक्षणसंयुतम्।।1.18.10।।

विष्णोरर्धं महाभागं पुत्रमैक्ष्वाकुवर्धनम्।

Six seasons (one year) passed after the completion of the sacrifice. In the twelfth month of **Chaitra** on the **ninth day (of the bright fortnight)**, with **Aditi** as presiding deity when the star **Punarvasu was in the ascendent** and the **five planets Sun, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter and Venus, were exalted in their own house in Karkaṭa lagna, when Bṛhaspati was in conjunction with the Moon,** Kausalyā gave birth to a son: a facet of Viṣṇu, Lord of the entire universe who received obeisance from all the worlds and was adorned with all auspicious signs, the venerable one to perpetuate the Ikṣvāku race.

Following is the chart which Paramguruji Sanjay Rath uses for Sri Rama.

Five planets - Su, Ma, Ve, Sa, Guru are ucca\~exalted while Mo is in own rasi\~sign. Rahu-Ketu are in 6-12 axis nica~debilitated.



![Rama's birth chart, Bala Kanda](../images/sri-rama-chart.png)



### Tithi

Born on Chaitra Śukla Navami: Navami is ruled by Sūrya. In his relationships, Śrī Rāma is very dharmic, proud and he upheld highest dharma in his marriage throughout. However because Sūrya is cursed by Śani, Rāhu and Maṅgala, it has resulted in separation, frustration, tests in marriage as well.

### Punarvasu: Janma~Birth nakshatra

Punarvasu = Punah + vasu = पुनः + वसु = again + radiance/light = restoration of glory, wealth, prosperity; one who rises again to goodness; have ability to bounce back.

So this nakshatra indicates sudden fall and rise. In the Vimshottari Dasa scheme, the nakshatra rulership is with Brihaspati~Guru.

The deity associated with Punarvasu is mother Aditi, wife of Kashyapa who gave birth to 33 devas (12 Adityas, 11 Rudras, 8 Vasu, Indra, Prajapati). So Punarvasu born are easy-going, easily satisfied, helpful, have good qualities and provide for others just as Aditi, the mother of all *devas.* These people may also be self-sacrificing, idealistic, religious, forgiving, honest, truthful - qualities we would associate with Guru Brihaspati.

Ramana Maharishi, Giorgio Armani, Harrison Ford, Theodore Roosevelt are some other people born in this nakshatra and can be seen to have a renewal, bouncing back theme in their lives. 

Punarvasu is a Cara~movable nakshatra, so in muhurta it is good for planning travels, acquiring vehicles or events which require movement. This nakshatra may also indicate travels, foreign visits or stays.This nakshatra is not suitable for marriages though it is good for renewing vows or getting back together after separation. 

There’s more depth to using nakshatra through Navtara and Sarvotabhadra scheme.

### Lagna: Karka~Cancer

Cancer Lagna~Ascendant people can be emotional-fickle; honor brahmins-religious people; are good with strategy; learned, intelligent; enduring and caring like a mother, honored for virtues; have a small or honorable family-lineage; may have less children or issues concerning children; consider friends as part of family.

Sri Ram comes from royal lineage-he is *Surya-vanshi*; has traditionally treated Brahmins with great reverence; emotional-he cried inconsolably for his wife before Rishi Agastya so much so that Siva had to appear and calm him by giving knowledge in form of Siva Gita; has had issues with children and undoubtedly honored for his dharma, virtues.

Lagna Lord in 1H in own rasi conjunct exalted Guru: Sri Ram has very high ideals about conducting himself in accordance with the prevalent dharma and by the words of the rishi-gurus being the 9L *\[SanjayRath].* 

Guru is one of the four graha who make a person intelligent and being 6L conjunct Lagna lord also forms Dhimanta yoga making Sri Ram very intelligent and wise. 

Also, Guru is 6L sitting in lagna, so gurus-rishis want service from him which is evident when Rishi Vishwamitra asked for him. 6H is also enemies, and 6L being exalted shows the mighty scholar Ravana being inimical to him. 

Guru Chandra conjunction in Lagna forms a beautiful Gaj-kesari yoga which makes him virtuous, granting him honors, wealth, and support from the society. They also form Laxmi-Narayan yoga on Lagna, so he’d have prosperity coming to him as part of his bhagya 9H. 

Guru is also digbali in Lagna in *Hamsa Mahapurusa* yoga, which shows complete blessings of *Isana* and Sri Ram’s incredible grasp on dharma, religion and vedic conduct. No wonder he is *maryada purushottama*.

However that Guru in Lagna is aspected by Sani and Mangala causing a curse onto him coming from past life. Devrishi Narada had cursed Visnu that he’d have to suffer the pain of separation from his beloved which became part of both Sri Ram and Krishna Avatara. So Sri Ram had to leave his birthplace~Lagna and wander in the forests. More details on this is taught by Pt Sanjay Rath in his various teachings.

### Chandra Lagna Chakra

10th from Chandra has ucca-exalted Surya indicating the society, the people want him to be the Kshatriya, to rule, to be the king and of all the Visnu avatar we all subconsciously understand Sri Rama to be the king of Bharata and so no wonder when temple at Rama-janmabhumi was inaugurated, everybody welcomed him by as king of Bharata.

With Ketu in 12th, troubles in marriage can be expected due to sudden events and continuation of lineage is the reason for getting married.

Mangala in 7th indicates he loves to hangout with his brothers, Sri Hanuman and male colleagues.

4H Sani indicates dangers but the ucca-exalted lord Sukra protects him and his wife Sita followed him into *vanvas*~exile to be with him even though such condition wasn’t placed on her.

More details are taught in PJC and Dhana Karaka workshop.

### Surya

Surya is ucca-exalted and its dispositor is also exalted. Surya is in a curse which resulted in Sri Ram to lose his throne. Right when he was about to be crowned as king certain events transpired which forced him into an exile. Surya in 10H is digbali shows he knows how to lead however cursed situation forced him to not be able to do so. But when he was with foreigners, vaanars and servants he did lead them with dharma. He regained his position as king of Ayodhya after the returning from Lanka however he still faced challenges in leading peacefully. But his ideals in leadership cannot be questioned. Surya is 2L in 10H showing he will take forward the karma of his lineage which is to rule like his forefathers. Surya is in Garvita and Dipta avastha as he’s born to lead men on path of dharma. 

### Mangala

Mangala is ucca-exalted but in Marana Karaka Sthana which indicates troubles in marital life and suffering to people fighting with him in war. 7H Mangala also forms Kuja dosha which isn’t conducive for marriage and will give troubles concerning intimacy. While this is not as bad as for someone like him, someone with very high dharma-ideals but in modern age it can spell disaster and fights, distress can be expected in marriage. Yet Sri Ram also had to fight for survival of his marriage and that area of life was most tested even after the Ramayana. Mangala is representing Sri Hanuman in his chart who came to his rescue and literally destroyed his enemies. Mangala is 5L in 7H indicating Sri Rama loved his wife dearly but it came with pain, wars and tests. Mangala has aspects of Rahu, Guru and Chandra showing underhanded methods in war and elevation of people working for him. Everyone who came to him directly or accidentally was uplifted out of their previous birth’s curses or raised to veneration like Sri Hanuman, Vibhishina, Jatayu, Shabri, Ahilya and more. Mangala is also in Garvita and Dipta avastha and benefic aspects make it better so he knows how to fight, what is the most dharmic way to fight even though it may appear (AL10) to be underhanded like killing of Bali or taking help of Vibhishana. Even in Gita 10.31 Krishna says,”*rāmaḥ śhastra-bhṛitām aham”*  - of the wielders of weapons I am Rāma, so there isn’t a warrior as big as Sri Rama. 

## Arudha

Arudha is what the world perceives about someone and about things associated with them.

Sri Rama’s Arudha Lagna is in 10H Aries with ucca Surya so undoubtedly we all perceive him as the king of Bharata, as a mighty leader and one upholding the dharma at its highest. 

Chandra, Sani and Mangala are digbali from Arudha lagna taking him to south for war, studying with Rishi Vashishtha and regaining glory due to Vayu-putra Hanuman.

He’s seen as mighty Kshtatriya in his karma due to Mangala in AL10. 

With Sukra in 12th, his own people have tarnished his reputation on account of his wife but it forms a subh-yoga so he lost his wife even after Ramayana to uphold the dharma of a king. 

Rahu is in 9th Marana karaka sthana from the Arudha Lagna so he got good support from outsiders all through the Ramayana who were in a disheartening situations personally in their lives when they met Rama like Sugriva, Sri Hanuman, Jatayu, Vibhishana and more.

Sri Rama’s second step-mother became inimical, is seen by A6 in 8H as one lord comes to 4H and the other lord Rahu, here Ravana, is in 6H nica-debilitated. 

From A4 we can see Sri Rama finds happiness being with his community, family and lineage. 

## Mula Dasa

Mula Dasa finds mention in Kalyan Verma’s Saravali and it is good for timing curses, hardships and other evils. It shows the exact period when a curse or blessing shall come into play. Sometimes painful experiences cannot be remedied but just have to be experienced, it is the dridha (fixed) karma we carry from past lives.

In Sri Ram’s chart, Mula Dasa is used to time and determine the length of his exile from Ayodhya which was a consequence of the curse of Devrishi Narada on Visnu as mentioned earlier. 

If you wish to learn to calculate Mula dasa, I’d suggest reading Pt Sanjay Rath’s article “Mūla Daśā” dated September 30, 2017.

From Mula dasa of Sri Rama, we can clearly see that during the exact 14 year period of Sani dasa (Sani is causing curse, delivering punishing karma of past life which in unflinching since it is retrograde), Sri Rama was exiled to forests and during this 14 year period he suffered from the pain of losing his beloved and subsequently being saved by a *vaanara*, Sri Hanuman.

**Om ṭat ṣat**
